encounter.place_of_service: Visit conducted by synchronous audio and video telehealth on a HIPAA-compliant platform. The client was located at client's home; the provider was located at provider's office. The client consented to receive care by telehealth.

assessment.formulation: Clinician stated: "Presentation stable and well controlled on the current dose. Work related anxiety with avoidance and rumination improving with cognitive behavioral work."
assessment.medical_necessity: Continued treatment is necessary to manage ADHD symptoms with medication and to address work-related anxiety and avoidance behaviors through cognitive behavioral therapy.

subjective.adherence: The client is taking methylphenidate 36 mg extended release every morning as prescribed. They report being careful to take it before 8:00 AM to avoid sleep disruption.
subjective.side_effects: The client denies headaches and heart racing. They report slight jitteriness the first week that has since resolved. They report decreased appetite at lunch. They deny sleep issues as long as the medication is taken early.
subjective.chief_complaint: The client stated, "it's been a rough couple of weeks" at work with a new manager, feeling like "everything I handed comes back with comments."
subjective.psychiatric_ros: Anxiety is present, specifically related to work. Sleep is adequate. Attention and focus are improved in the mornings but drift in the afternoons when the medication wears off. Psychosis is denied.
subjective.interval_history: The client reports that methylphenidate is mostly good, helping them get through their inbox, though it wears off around 4:00 PM causing slight fogginess. They report significant work-related anxiety triggered by a new manager's feedback, leading to automatic thoughts of incompetence, avoidance behaviors (delaying email replies), and evening rumination. Sleep is adequate (6.5 to 7 hours) and restful if medication is taken before 8:00 AM. Appetite is reduced at lunch, but weight remains stable. Home blood pressure was checked and reported as 124/78.

current_medications: methylphenidate 36 milligram extended release every morning

psychotherapy.progress: The client demonstrated progress by successfully negotiating flexible hours on Fridays (a previous goal) and showing a reduction in in-session anxiety (from 85 to 40, and 8 to 4) when evaluating thoughts objectively.
psychotherapy.response: The client engaged well, successfully identified evidence contrary to their negative thoughts, recognized their cognitive distortions, and agreed to implement the behavioral experiments and structural changes.
psychotherapy.goal_plan: The client will conduct an email reply experiment (replying within two hours or by the end of the day, writing predictions and actual outcomes), schedule a 15-minute worry time at 7:00 PM, stop checking work emails after 7:00 PM, run twice a week (Tuesday and Saturday), and practice noticing the "not trying hard enough" story.
psychotherapy.issues_addressed: Work-related anxiety, cognitive distortions (catastrophizing, mind reading, mental filter), avoidance behaviors (delaying email replies), evening rumination, and a core belief of "not trying hard enough" stemming from childhood ADHD experiences.
psychotherapy.psychotherapy_time: Start time: Not stated. End time: Not stated. Minutes: 18 minutes.
psychotherapy.modality_interventions: Cognitive behavioral therapy. Interventions included identifying automatic thoughts, completing a thought record to examine evidence for and against negative beliefs, identifying cognitive distortions, setting up a behavioral experiment for email replies, scheduling a dedicated worry time, and running the "movie to the end" to de-catastrophize worst-case scenarios.

substance_use.alcohol: A beer or two on the weekend.
